items.headline: Sensex falls 319 points to 81,592.45 and Nifty 0.61% to 25,144.30 on inflation and oil worries
items.summary: Autos, metals, realty and financials led Friday's selling after October inflation of 6.09% and a rebound in crude. Both indices still posted a third straight weekly gain. Rally pausing after Thursday's flat close.
items.rationale: Inflation above the RBI's ceiling raises rate-hike odds and hits rate-sensitive sectors first; costlier oil and higher US yields add pressure after a steep November rally.

items.headline: Foreign investors buy a net ₹5,736.55 crore on Friday; domestic funds sell ₹2,253.58 crore
items.summary: Provisional exchange data show foreign buying continued despite the index fall, after ₹7,831 crore on Thursday. Ongoing: November inflows have been the strongest stretch in months.
items.rationale: Sustained foreign buying cushions equities and the rupee against higher US yields and oil, though domestic funds keep selling into the rally.

economies.why: Buying persists on a down day

items.headline: Rupee falls 8 paise to 94.20 per dollar as the dollar index hits its highest since April 2025
items.summary: It opened at 94.07 and closed provisionally at 94.20, a second straight fall. Traders cited hot US inflation, rising Treasury yields, hawkish Fed remarks and weak equities. Reversing last week's gains.
items.rationale: A firmer dollar and costlier crude outweigh foreign equity inflows, raising imported inflation and hedging costs.

items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield rises about 5 bps to 7.30% on higher US yields and supply worries
items.summary: The benchmark closed near 7.30–7.31% on Friday, up from 7.25%, on rising US Treasury yields and concern over extra bond supply. Escalating: up from 7.19% a week ago.
items.rationale: Higher sovereign yields lift borrowing costs for the government and companies and bring mark-to-market losses on banks' bond books.

economies.why: Yield up 11 bps in a week

items.headline: Economists see the repo rate at 6% by February after inflation breaches the RBI's band
items.summary: Most forecasters expect 25 bps in December and again in February from 5.50%; one large lender's research arm cut its December call to 25 bps from 50 and opposes a February hike. New after Thursday's 6.09% print.
items.rationale: A longer tightening path raises loan and deposit rates, slowing credit-led demand, though a smaller December move than feared limits the shock.

items.headline: October goods exports hit a record $49.47 billion, up 45%, but the goods deficit widens to $39.88 billion
items.summary: Imports rose to $89.35 billion; the goods gap is a one-year high and above the $32.25 billion forecast. Including services, the overall deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion from $25.15 billion a year earlier. New data.
items.rationale: Record exports support growth and manufacturing, but a wider goods gap driven by costly imports adds dollar demand and weighs on the rupee.

items.headline: Forex reserves rise $2.49 billion to $719.55 billion in the week to 6 November
items.summary: Gold holdings rose about $2.2 billion to $104.8 billion; foreign currency assets edged up $232 million to $591.35 billion. Reverses the previous week's $2.69 billion fall.
items.rationale: A larger reserve buffer gives the RBI more room to smooth rupee swings as the dollar strengthens.

items.headline: Brent holds near $96 but heads for a second weekly fall of about 2% as the US keeps its Iran blockade
items.summary: Brent traded around $95.5–96.5 on Friday with WTI near $88, after Thursday's 3.3% jump. Iran denied talks with Washington. Rebound from Tuesday's dip below $90 is holding.
items.rationale: Crude back in the mid-$90s keeps India's import bill, fuel under-recoveries and inflation risk high just as CPI has breached 6%.

items.headline: Iran's Guards say two oil supertankers and an LNG tanker were disabled by mines in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran said the ships used an 'unauthorised' route; outbound Hormuz transits fell sharply and Iran ruled out nuclear inspections while under US threat. Escalating after record October attacks.
items.rationale: Mines add a new hazard on the route carrying much of India's crude and LNG, raising freight, insurance and supply risk as Gulf barrels overtake Russian supply.

items.headline: US 10-year yield touches 5.17% and the dollar index 103.38 as markets price a December Fed hike
items.summary: The 2-year yield rose about 35 bps on the week, its biggest jump since September 2024, after Fed officials warned on inflation. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% on Friday. Escalating from Wednesday's hot CPI.
items.rationale: Higher US yields and a stronger dollar narrow India's yield advantage, threatening foreign inflows and pushing up the rupee's cost of defence and domestic yields.

items.headline: Nasdaq falls 0.9% as chip and AI stocks slide after a leading chipmaker's chief resigns
items.summary: The Nasdaq-100 lost 1.22%, the weakest major US index on Friday, though the S&P 500 still gained 2.5% for the week. New.
items.rationale: A sell-off in US technology shares tends to spill into Indian IT stocks at Monday's open and can dent sentiment on AI-linked spending.

items.headline: US assures India of tariffs below those on rival exporters as trade talks target a first-phase deal
items.summary: Reports say Washington promised India a tariff edge over peers; both sides aim to conclude a first phase by next month's G20 summit. Easing, despite this week's US duties on Indian solar panels.
items.rationale: A relative tariff advantage would help labour-intensive exporters win US orders; details and timing remain unconfirmed.
